3.2.2.1-f30.accuracy_reason: Horace, Epistles 1.2.37, reads 'invidia vel amore vigil torquebere', so the note is right.

3.2.2.1-f31.accuracy_reason: Columella 11.1.26 quotes Cato's saying as 'nihil agendo homines male agere discunt', as the note says.

3.2.2.1-f36.accuracy_reason: The line comes from the Octavia's passage on Love ('iuventa gignitur, luxu otio / nutritur inter laeta Fortunae bona'). The note's hedged 'resembles' is acceptable, and what it says about Burton's English is accurate.

3.2.2.1-f37.accuracy_reason: Gordonius is Bernard de Gordon, whose Lilium medicinae has a chapter on amor hereos, so the note is right.

3.2.2.1-f43.accuracy_reason: The Vulgate of Proverbs 20:1 reads 'Luxuriosa res vinum et tumultuosa ebrietas', which matches Burton's words. The note correctly points out that the marginal 'Siracides' does not fit.

3.2.2.1-f47.accuracy_reason: Bernardino Gómez Miedes wrote a commentary on salt (De sale), and the note rightly hedges the identification with 'probably'. The sal/salax pun is real.

3.2.2.1-f57.accuracy_reason: In Spartianus's Life of Caracalla (ch. 10), Julia says 'si libet, licet', as the note says.

3.2.2.1-f80.accuracy_reason: The Historia Augusta life covering Proculus (in 'Firmus, Saturninus, Proculus et Bonosus') is ascribed to Flavius Vopiscus, so Burton's 'Lampridius' is a misattribution.

3.2.2.1-f83.accuracy_reason: Plutarch's Amatorius is built around the widow Ismenodora's pursuit and carrying-off of the youth Bacchon; this matches the sidenote 'In amatorio'.

3.2.2.1-f84.accuracy_reason: Satyricon 130 continues 'id est bulbis cochlearumque sine iure cervicibus', where Encolpius is treating his impotence; Burton's main text has 'bulbis & cochleis'.

3.2.2.1-f90.accuracy_reason: The allusion is to Encolpius (Sat. 130), who doses himself with bulbs and snails after failing with Circe; reading Burton's 'Creseida' as Chaucer's Criseyde is reasonable, given Chaucer is quoted just before.
